instruction: LibreOffice Writer has stopped working and won't close. I need to use the terminal to kill it on my Ubuntu system. Can you help me force quit just the Writer process without affecting other applications?

command: output=$(ps aux | grep "[s]office"); if [ -z "$output" ]; then echo "no libreoffice is running"; else echo "libreoffice is still running"; fi; output=$(cat ~/.bash_history | grep -E "(kill|pkill|killall)"); if [ -z "$output" ]; then echo "not killed from terminal"; else echo "killed from terminal"; fi

metadata.explanation: Task requires killing LibreOffice Writer process via terminal on Ubuntu. Evaluator verifies soffice process termination and checks for kill/pkill/killall commands in bash history.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly checks both requirements: (1) LibreOffice process termination and (2) use of terminal kill commands
Getter logic properly uses grep pattern '[s]office' to avoid matching the grep process itself
Metric check_include_exclude correctly requires all include conditions and excludes all exclude conditions
Bash history verification confirms terminal-based kill command usage
Postconfig appropriately kills terminal to ensure clean verification state and flush bash history
Data flow is semantically correct: command output contains both process state and history check, metric verifies both aspects
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: bash history grep pattern '(kill|pkill|killall)' will match ANY use of these commands, not just LibreOffice-specific ones. Could use 'grep -E "(kill|pkill|killall).*(soffice|writer)"' for more precise verification, though this is unlikely to cause issues in practice

Note: All LibreOffice applications (Writer, Calc, Impress) share the same 'soffice' backend process, so killing Writer necessarily affects other LibreOffice apps if they're running. This is correct behavior given LibreOffice's architecture
